problem.title: Pump failure prediction
problem.context: A water utility runs about 400 pumps in 12 pumping stations. Each pump has vibration, temperature and pressure sensors reporting every second. Unexpected failures interrupt water supply. The utility wants predictive maintenance; several stations have unreliable mobile connections, there are two data scientists, and IT supports servers and networks.

requirements.text: Warn the maintenance team at least 24 hours before a pump is likely to fail, naming the pump and the probable cause.
Improve the predictions as technicians record what they find at each inspection.
When a station loses its connection for up to two days, warnings for its pumps still reach the station’s on-call technician.
When a new pump model is installed, its pumps get predictions within one month, without changes to how the other pumps are scored.
Sensor data stays on the utility’s own premises: no cloud service may store or process it.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Shared fleet model
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, a shared fleet model performs inference at the edge and produces warnings locally. Alerts are queued locally when offline, while inspection labels are sent to a central process for retraining the shared model. Trade-off: This provides prompt, locally available warnings and lets inspection data improve one common model across the fleet. Trade-off: The shared model may be less tailored to individual stations, and improvements depend on centrally retraining and distributing updated models.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: The station edge runs model-family plugins with calibration, producing predictions locally and placing warnings in an alert queue when offline. Inspection labels are sent centrally to retrain the models, whose updated versions and calibration can later be deployed to stations. Trade-off: This provides low-latency, outage-tolerant warnings and modular model replacement, but requires managing plugins and model versions across stations, while retraining feedback is delayed and depends on inspection labels.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Independent model per pump family
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Federated station updates
points.description: The system runs a separate pump-family model at each station edge, using local data for inference. It generates alerts locally and queues them during connectivity loss, while federated station updates periodically improve models without centralizing raw data. Trade-off: This gains low-latency, locally resilient warning and preserves station-level data locality. It gives up the simplicity of one centralized model and requires coordinating multiple family models and federated updates.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Shared fleet model with local fallback rules
Offline warning path: Local model with rule fallback
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: The shared fleet model runs at the station edge for timely pump-failure predictions, with local fallback rules when needed. During offline operation, a local model continues inference and falls back to rules; inspection labels are sent centrally for retraining. Trade-off: This gains low-latency, resilient warnings and fleet-wide learning from inspection data. It gives up immediate adaptation to station-specific behavior and depends on maintaining local models and rules while central retraining catches up.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, family-specific model plugins run locally, with calibration applied to their outputs. Local inference places warnings in an alert queue during offline operation, while inspection labels support versioned, per-family retraining. Trade-off: This improves offline responsiveness, model-family adaptability, and traceable updates. It gives up centralized simplicity and increases station-side deployment and maintenance burden, while calibration and separate retraining may require additional operational coordination.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Offline warning path: Local model with rule fallback
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, family-specific model plugins run at the edge and apply calibration to produce predictions. A local warning model operates offline, falling back to rules when needed, while inspection labels drive versioned retraining separately for each model family. Trade-off: This gains low-latency, resilient warnings and lets families be updated and audited independently. It gives up centralized simplicity: plugin, calibration, fallback, and per-family version management increase operational complexity, while retraining depends on the availability and quality of inspection labels.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Shared fleet model with local fallback rules
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, a shared fleet model runs at the edge, with local fallback rules handling cases when normal model operation is unavailable. The station performs inference offline, queues alerts locally, and sends inspection labels to central retraining to improve the shared model. Trade-off: This provides low-latency, connectivity-tolerant warnings and fleet-wide learning, but requires coordinating model updates and queued alerts across stations and may delay learning from inspections until synchronization.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Offline warning path: Local model with rule fallback
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: Pump data is evaluated at the station edge using a selected model-family plugin and its calibration. When offline, the local model continues issuing warnings and falls back to rules, while inspection labels are sent to central retraining to improve future model releases. Trade-off: This provides low-latency, offline-capable warnings and supports multiple calibrated model families, but requires managing model and calibration versions at stations. Central retraining can improve accuracy from inspections, at the cost of updates depending on collected labels and deployment to the edge.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Independent model per pump family
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, a pump-family-specific model runs locally, producing predictions and placing warnings in a local alert queue. Inspection labels are later centralized to retrain the independent family models, which are then redeployed to stations. Trade-off: This provides low-latency, locally available warnings and allows models to specialize by pump family. It gives up centralized simplicity and requires coordinating deployments and retraining across multiple models; learning also depends on inspection labels arriving centrally.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Independent model per pump family
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, a pump-family-specific model runs locally to infer failure risk. Warnings are placed in a local alert queue, while inspection labels support versioned retraining independently for each pump family. Trade-off: This reduces dependence on connectivity and allows family-specific model updates, but increases deployment and version-management overhead across stations and families. It also relies on inspection labels, so learning may be slower or uneven where inspections are sparse.

values: Inference placement: Station edge
Model organization: Shared fleet model with local fallback rules
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
points.description: At each station, a shared fleet model runs at the edge, with local fallback rules maintaining decisions when the model is unavailable. Offline warnings are handled by local inference and an alert queue, while inspection labels drive versioned retraining for each equipment family. Trade-off: This combines low-latency, outage-tolerant alerts with centrally organized learning, but requires managing model versions, family-specific retraining, and possible differences between shared-model outputs and local fallback behavior.

approaches.idea: What if one shared fleet model runs at station edges and learns centrally from inspection labels?
What if calibrated model-family plugins isolate scoring and updates?
What if each pump family has an independent edge model with federated station updates?
What if edge models retain a rule fallback for degraded operation?

adrs.title: Where inference runs and warnings remain available
adrs.context: Sensor processing must stay on utility premises, and warnings must reach station technicians through a two-day connection loss. Station-edge inference with a local warning path satisfies both demands; the remaining choice is whether the offline path also includes local rule fallback.

options.name: Station edge with queued local inference
values: Inference placement: Station edge
Offline warning path: Local inference and alert queue
pros: Generates and queues warnings during network loss.
cons: Does not describe a fallback when model inference itself is unavailable.
options.reason: Chosen by the shared and independent family model alternatives.

options.name: Station edge with model and rule fallback
values: Inference placement: Station edge
Offline warning path: Local model with rule fallback
pros: Provides a local fallback warning path.
cons: Requires maintaining local rules alongside model versions.
options.reason: Chosen by alternatives that prioritize a fallback path during degraded operation.

adrs.title: How pump models and inspection learning are organized
adrs.context: Predictions need to identify likely failures, improve from inspection findings, and allow a new pump model to receive predictions without changing other pumps’ scoring. Shared models simplify fleet learning, while family-specific plugins or models isolate scoring and updates.

options.name: Shared fleet model with family-versioned learning
values: Model organization: Shared fleet model with local fallback rules
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
pros: Inspection labels can improve a fleet-wide model.
Versioned family retraining supports controlled updates.
cons: New-family work may still affect shared model management.
options.reason: Chosen when fleet-wide reuse of inspection learning is preferred.

options.name: Calibrated family plugins with versioned retraining
values: Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Learning loop: Versioned per-family retraining from inspection labels
pros: Provides traceable per-family updates from inspection findings.
cons: Adds plugin, calibration, and version management across stations.
options.reason: Chosen when onboarding isolation and controlled family updates are primary.

options.name: Independent family models with central retraining
values: Model organization: Independent model per pump family
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
pros: Offers a direct central inspection-label learning loop.
options.reason: Chosen for family independence while using a straightforward on-premises learning pipeline.

options.name: Calibrated family plugins with central retraining
values: Model organization: Model-family plugins with calibration
Learning loop: Central retraining from inspection labels
pros: Keeps retraining centrally managed on premises.
cons: Updates are less explicitly versioned per family.
options.reason: Chosen for isolated scoring with a simpler central feedback pipeline.

options.name: Federated station updates
values: Model organization: Independent model per pump family
Learning loop: Federated station updates
pros: Can update models using station-local training data.
cons: Requires coordinating federated updates, and inspection findings do not automatically translate into improved deployed predictions.
options.reason: Set aside because the learning effect and coordination burden are less direct for this utility.
